title: A first collaboration conversation with STXBP1 Foundation

sentences.text: On behalf of SLC6A1 Connect UK / Arthur's Quest, I propose exploring what our communities could learn together.
Evidence suggests that some SLC6A1 and STXBP1 variants produce unstable or incorrectly folded proteins, but this shared connection is contested and does not cover every variant.
The atlas also infers similar symptoms, including seizures with sudden loss of muscle tone, but its confidence is 0.46, below 0.5.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: SLC6A1 resources include the COMBINEDBrain / Across Matrix natural history platform, Simons Searchlight, Citizen Health and the COMBINEDBrain Biorepository.
STARR follows STXBP1-related disorders over time; we could explore sharing study designs and experience rather than assuming eligibility transfers.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: SLC6A1 clears the brain messenger GABA after release; shared protein-folding problems do not mean identical pathways.
We should read both supporting and limiting evidence: some SLC6A1 proteins reach the cell surface but work poorly, and an STXBP1 exception increases activity.
Please help confirm whether generalized myoclonic-atonic seizures, eyelid myoclonus and absence seizures occur in STXBP1-related disorders.
We could invite Scott Demarest, whose work covers both disorders, to review the plan.
Before joining forces, we should also check model access and the variant-specific protein-folding questions below.
Send STXBP1 Foundation one enquiry asking whether STARR could include SLC6A1-related disorders, without presuming expansion is possible.
Is there a documented, accessible SLC6A1 animal or cell model in the atlas?
Which GBA1, HEXA, NPC1 and GAA variants might respond to a protein-folding helper, as GLA variants are classified for migalastat?
Any treatment discussion should concern published evidence to discuss with a neurologist, not a recommendation.
Dear STXBP1 Foundation team,
Could we explore a small collaboration for our communities?
STARR currently studies STXBP1-related disorders.
Would you consider whether it could include SLC6A1-related disorders?
We would welcome an initial discussion of feasibility and evidence gaps.
[Your name], on behalf of SLC6A1 Connect UK / Arthur's Quest
